'''Oliver Chinganya''' {{Postnom|country=GBR|CStat}}is a Zambian [[chartered Statistician|chartered statistician]] (since 1999), [[chartered Scientist]] and a fellow of the [[Royal Statistical Society]]. He currently serves as the director of [[African Centre for Statistics]] at [[UN Economic Commission for Africa]] (UNECA).<ref>{{cite web |date=16 January 2020 |title=Economic Commission for Africa (ECA) and Zimbabwe sign agreement |url=https://www.thezimbabwemail.com/economic-analysis/economic-commission-for-africa-eca-and-zimbabwe-sign-agreement/ |website=[[The Mail (Zimbabwe)]] |access-date=16 May 2023 |archive-date=25 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125091241/https://www.thezimbabwemail.com/economic-analysis/economic-commission-for-africa-eca-and-zimbabwe-sign-agreement/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He is also serving as the Vice President of the [[International Statistical Institute]].<ref>{{cite web |last1= |first1= |date=24 March 2023 |title=More investment in data and statistics needed in Africa |url=https://african.business/2023/03/infocus/more-investment-in-data-and-statistics-needed-in-africa |website=[[African Business]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Oliver Chinganya |url=https://cepei.org/en/conferencistas/oliver-chinganya/ |website=Cepei}}</ref>

== Education ==
He was born in [[Livingstone, Zambia]].<ref name=":0" /> After graduating from secondary school, he joined the [[Zambian Statistics Agency]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1984, he enrolled in a training program sponsored by the [[UN Population Fund]].<ref name=":0" /> He earned the equivalent of a bachelor's degree from the [[Eastern Africa Statistical Training Centre]] at the [[University of Dar es Salaam]].<ref name=":0" /> He earned an [[M.Sc]] in Statistics from [[Southampton University]] in 1991, and later an [[MBA]] in [[Strategic Management]] from [[Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology]] in 2008.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Under Oliver Chinganya's leadership, the African Centre for Statistics is spearheading improvements in systems and training. |url=https://crvssystems.ca/sites/default/files/assets/images/CRVS_Leader_Ethiopia_e.pdf |website=Centre of Excellence for CRVS Systems}}</ref>

== Career ==
His career involved in the field of statistics and statistical development in Africa.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Anaja |first1=Hauwa Abubakar |date=24 March 2023 |title=SDGs: ECA Calls for Investment in Data and Statistics |url=https://von.gov.ng/sdgs-eca-calls-for-investment-in-data-and-statistics/ |newspaper=[[Voice of Nigeria]]}}</ref> He served as UNECA's Officer in Charge for the Climate Change, Environment and Natural Resources Management Division, and also set up the Digital Centre of Excellence.<ref>{{cite web |title=UN entities support ethiopias quest for policy coherence for sdgs |url=https://www.busiweek.com/un-entities-support-ethiopias-quest-for-policy-coherence-for-sdgs/ |url-status=usurped |website=[[East African Business Week]] |access-date=2023-05-16 |archive-date=2023-05-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230508070747/https://www.busiweek.com/un-entities-support-ethiopias-quest-for-policy-coherence-for-sdgs/ }}</ref>

Currently, Chinganya serves as the director of the African Centre for Statistics at the UN Economic Commission for Africa.<ref>{{cite web |date=9 August 2021 |title=CRVS systems fragilized by COVID-19 across Africa, says ECA's Chinganya - World |url=https://reliefweb.int/report/world/crvs-systems-fragilized-covid-19-across-africa-says-eca-s-chinganya |website=[[ReliefWeb]] |publisher=[[OCHA]] |language=en}}</ref>

Chinganya emphasized the importance of integrated [[civil registration]] and [[ID management]] and also highlighted the significance of civil registration as the foundation for collecting data from birth to death.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hersey |first1=Frank |date=31 October 2022 |title=UNECA and African experts urge civil registration to enable good governance |url=https://www.biometricupdate.com/202210/uneca-and-african-experts-urge-civil-registration-to-enable-good-governance |website=Biometric Update}}</ref>

In 2020, he bemoaned the negative impact of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa|COVID-19 pandemic]] on civil registration and vital statistics systems,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mavhunga |first1=Columbus |title=UN: Half of African Children Are Unregistered |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/africa_un-half-african-children-are-unregistered/6177628.html |website=[[Voice of America]] |language=en |date=15 October 2019}}</ref> particularly in Africa, leading to the absence of vital data.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kunambura |first1=Andrew |date=2021-04-30 |title=Africa to revolutionise civil registration systems |url=https://www.newsday.co.zw/news/article/32624/africa-to-revolutionise-civil-registration-systems |website=[[NewsDay (Zimbabwean newspaper)]] |language=en}}</ref>
